$comment: Patches applied to the vendored pylabview WHEN THE BUNDLE IS ASSEMBLED, never to vendor/ itself.
That keeps VENDOR.md's 'local changes: none' true of the vendored tree, so an upstream fix can
still be taken by copying the package over it. provision.ps1 applies these; a Find string that
does not occur EXACTLY ONCE is a hard error, because the failure mode to avoid is a patch that
silently stops matching after an upstream change and leaves the bug back in.
ANCHOR A FIND SO THAT THE UPSTREAM FIX BREAKS IT. A Find matching a line upstream's own fix
leaves untouched will keep applying after that fix lands, stacking a redundant change and
raising no error - which is the exact drift these entries claim to prevent. Span the lines the
Each entry: File relative to app/, Find and Replace as exact strings, Why, and Upstream.

patches.replace:
tdProbeTable = self.getTopType(probeTable_typeId, section_num=section_num)
        if tdProbeTable is not None and tdProbeTable.fullType() != TD_FULL_TYPE.RepeatedBlock:
            if (self.po.verbose > 1):
                eprint("{:s}: Warning: ProbeTable TD has unexpected type {:s}, treating as not found"
                       .format(self.vi.src_fname, tdProbeTable.fullType().name))
            tdProbeTable = None
        # Comment ProbeTable
patches.why: getNumRepeats() is called on the probe table without checking that it IS a RepeatedBlock. Only TDObjectRepeatedBlock defines that method, so a VI whose probe table resolves to a Cluster, Number or NumberPtr dies with AttributeError and extracts NOTHING - readRSRC exits 1 with zero files, not a partial bundle. The crash is in cosmetic code (setPurposeText and setDataFillComments only add XML comments), so no content was ever beyond reach. Measured on a production codebase: 32 of 900 VIs, all with this one cause - 28 Cluster, 3 NumberPtr, 1 Number - all of them DQMH module VIs. AN EARLIER VERSION OF THIS NOTE ADDED 'which is why NI's own example corpus never hit it'. That is false, and it mattered, because it made the bug sound like it needed a customer's code to see. It does not: the DQMH examples SHIPPED WITH LABVIEW reproduce it on a stock install - measured 2026-08-25 by swapping this file for the vendored original, on examples/Delacor/Delacor QMH/DQMH Fundamentals - Thermal Chamber/Libraries/Device Under Test_Cloneable_DQMH/Addressed to This Module.vi: upstream exits 1 with 0 files and an AttributeError, patched exits 0 with 19 files. Swept whole: 108 of the 240 VIs under vi.lib/Delacor and examples/Delacor are affected - 45%, against 3.6% in the production codebase - and they show FOUR wrong types, not three: 101 Cluster, 5 Ptr, 1 Boolean, 1 AlignedBlock. Ptr, Boolean and AlignedBlock are types no probe table could legitimately be, which is the strongest evidence yet that probeTable_typeId simply lands on an arbitrary entry. The earlier census never walked the add-on example trees. THE FORM BELOW IS THE MAINTAINER'S OWN, taken verbatim from his reply on issue #40 (2026-08-25): normalise tdProbeTable to None where it is resolved, and warn at verbose > 1 naming the file and the unexpected type. It is behaviourally identical to the guard-at-use form it replaces - tdProbeTable has no other consumer in commentSpecialTypes - but the warning is not cosmetic: he reads three different wrong types as evidence that the probeTable_typeId computation or the DSINIT entry positions are wrong for some versions, not that probe tables legitimately vary. Under that reading a silent guard hides a real bug, while -vv prints the evidence needed to chase it. TD_FULL_TYPE is imported function-locally at LVblock.py:5841 and eprint at module level, so the snippet compiles where it sits.
patches.upstream: reported as mefistotelis/pylabview#40; the maintainer approved this form but said he is not willing to spend time on it, so it may sit unmerged. Remove this entry once it lands upstream - the Find spans the two lines his fix inserts between, so provision will fail loudly rather than stack a second guard.
